title: Accessibility, internationalisation and usability — agent-panel evaluation

panel_protocol.limitation: Source-verified and fixture-proven implementation only; golden plain/JSON/JSONL snapshot suites, external localized message catalogue packs, and live assistive technology/information-specialist participant trials remain gated.

inter_rater_agreement.agreement_notes: All three panel roles converged independently on approval (scores: 0.98, 0.97, 0.98; consensus score: 0.98). Convergence centered on: (1) Deterministic, accessible diagnostic rendering in searchright_diagnostics::render and render_plain guaranteeing zero ANSI escape sequences, explicit word-based severity headers (BLOCKING, ERROR, WARNING, INFO), vertical hierarchy independent of terminal-width/wrapping, and complete elimination of unlabelled unicode glyphs; (2) Lossless round-tripping of machine-readable JSON and JSONL representations with stable lexical sorting across five keys; (3) Clean architectural separation of stable machine codes and severities from human-facing text during message catalogue localization (DiagnosticMessageCatalog, localize); (4) Fail-closed (Reject) versus source-preserving (PreserveSource) fallback policies for missing catalogue entries; (5) Robust BCP 47 locale typing (DiagnosticLocale) with enforced hyphen validation on custom tags; (6) Strict external evaluation protocol contracts (evaluation/external-evaluation.json) mandating at least 2 independent information specialists, exclusion of the developer team from adjudication, mandatory conflict disclosure, crossover strata, and sealed benchmark labels; (7) Compliance with non-negotiable Searchright rules maintaining PRISMA-S as a reporting contract and prohibiting autonomous screening exclusion; and (8) Honest preservation of all three open maturity gates (plain/JSON/JSONL snapshots, message catalogue translation packs, and participant usability evaluation) without premature completion claims.
convergence_vectors: Accessible PlainText rendering eliminating all ANSI escape sequences (\u{1b}) and standalone unlabelled glyphs (⚠, ✗, ✓, ⛔)
Explicit uppercase word-based severity headers (BLOCKING, ERROR, WARNING, INFO) eliminating color and icon dependencies
Terminal-width and line-wrapping independence via vertical hierarchical diagnostic formatting
Bidirectional serialization fidelity and deterministic sorting across PlainText, JSON, and JSONL formats
Strict invariance of machine identifiers (code, severity, blocking, evidence_ids) across message catalogue localization
Configurable MissingMessagePolicy supporting fail-closed Reject and source-preserving PreserveSource modes
BCP 47 structured locale tagging with hyphen validation for custom language codes
Usability evaluation independence contracts requiring >= 2 independent information specialists and developer team exclusion
Mandatory evaluator conflict-of-interest disclosure and sealed evaluation labels
PRISMA-S maintained strictly as an auditable reporting contract and not an autonomous conduct standard
Status of external evaluation locked to prepared_not_preregistered with null self-attestation receipts
divergence_vectors: Appropriate tooling for automated snapshot testing across simulated screen reader buffers versus raw terminal pipes
Prioritisation of community-sourced Indigenous language translation catalogues (e.g. te reo Māori) alongside official jurisdictional packs

verified_invariants: zero ANSI escape sequences: plain text rendering contains no terminal color, cursor positioning, or escape sequences (\u{1b})
word-based severity headers: all diagnostic messages begin with explicit textual severity tokens (BLOCKING, ERROR, WARNING, INFO)
terminal-width and wrapping independence: output uses clean vertical hierarchy without relying on fixed column widths, carriage returns (\r), or tabular clipping
unlabelled glyph elimination: standalone unicode symbols (⚠, ✗, ✓, ⛔) are forbidden without explicit text equivalents
strict control character rejection: contract validation rejects non-printable ASCII control characters in human messages and remediations
deterministic output sorting: diagnostics are ordered consistently by severity descending, code ascending, path ascending, line ascending, and column ascending
bidirectional machine format round-tripping: JSON and JSONL outputs serialize and deserialize losslessly against Diagnostic contracts
fail-closed validation: invalid contracts (zero lines, line-less columns, mismatched blocking flags, non-namespaced codes) fail validation before rendering
invariant machine identifiers: diagnostic codes, severities, blocking flags, and evidence IDs remain bitwise identical across locale translations
strict separation of machine semantics and human presentation: message catalogues only mutate message, remediation, and locale attributes
fail-closed or source-preserving missing message policy: MissingMessagePolicy::Reject returns MissingMessage error while PreserveSource retains canonical text
structured BCP 47 locale representation: DiagnosticLocale supports en-AU, en-NZ, en-US, mi-NZ, and validated hyphenated BCP 47 custom strings
deterministic catalog lookup: DiagnosticMessageCatalog uses BTreeMap ensuring reproducible iteration and evaluation order
post-translation contract validation: translated diagnostics re-run full contract validation to prevent invalid control characters in localized text
custom locale hyphen requirement: DiagnosticLocale::Custom must contain a hyphen, preventing malformed language codes
independent adjudication: minimum of 2 independent information specialists required with developer team strictly excluded from adjudication
mandatory conflict disclosure: all evaluator and provider relationships must be explicitly recorded before participant recruitment
sealed benchmark labels: evaluation design mandates sealed labels to prevent prompt gaming, fixture leakage, and benchmark overfitting
crossover multi-strata evaluation: protocol enforces balanced representation across clinical, economic, policy, and scoping review domains
PRISMA-S reporting contract: PRISMA-S is treated strictly as an auditable reporting contract and never represented as an autonomous conduct standard
pre-registration boundary: evaluation contract status is locked to prepared_not_preregistered; self-attestation of external evidence is forbidden
no autonomous screening exclusion: human-in-the-loop sign-off is preserved across all screening and governance contracts
honest claim boundaries: source-verified diagnostic contracts are clearly distinguished from live participant trials and ethics-approved evaluation execution

assertions_evaluated.notes: Stable lower-case namespaced diagnostic codes (code.contains('.')), four-level severity model, mandatory remediation for blocking diagnostics, and control-character rejection verified by 22 Rust tests and Python test_diagnostic_example_conforms_to_schema_and_invariants.

Plain text, JSON, and JSONL multi-format rendering in searchright_diagnostics::render verified; round-trip deserialization, deterministic sorting, and zero ANSI sequences proven in test_multiformat_accessible_rendering_plain_json_jsonl.

Separable message catalogues, MissingMessagePolicy (PreserveSource and Reject), DiagnosticLocale variants (EnAu, EnNz, EnUs, MiNz, Custom), and machine code invariance proven in test_locale_neutrality_and_message_separation and test_message_catalogue_localization_and_fallback_policies.

Accessible plain text design contracts eliminating ANSI sequences, terminal-width dependencies, carriage returns, and unlabelled glyphs verified in searchright_diagnostics::render_plain and test_accessible_rendering_contracts.

Information-specialist usability protocol, 2-specialist minimum independence, developer adjudication exclusion, conflict disclosure, and sealed labels verified by test_information_specialist_usability_protocol and evaluation/external-evaluation.json.

findings.description: Deterministic plain text, JSON, and JSONL rendering are verified across unit and integration tests; compiling and running exhaustive golden snapshot suites across varied terminal dimensions remains an open maturity gate.
findings.recommendation: Preserve gate T27-G-SNAPSHOTS-AND-NO-COLOUR open until snapshot test harnesses are integrated.

findings.description: severity_label maps DiagnosticSeverity to unambiguous string words (INFO, WARNING, ERROR, BLOCKING), ensuring assistive technologies read explicit categories rather than relying on color coding or auditory beeps.
findings.recommendation: Maintain explicit word headers across all CLI, MCP, and library diagnostic projections.

findings.description: reject_control_characters in crates/searchright-contracts/src/diagnostic.rs prevents ANSI escapes and terminal injection attacks by forbidding ASCII control codes except standard whitespace (\n and \t).
findings.recommendation: Retain control character stripping and validation in all user-supplied text inputs.

findings.description: Message catalogue localization, fallback policies, and invariant machine code retention are proved with test Māori and English catalogues; comprehensive production message catalogue packs across additional jurisdictions remain an open maturity gate.
findings.recommendation: Preserve gate T27-G-MESSAGE-CATALOGUES-FALLBACK open until community-reviewed translation packs are published.

findings.description: MissingMessagePolicy::Reject enables fail-closed localization validation in jurisdictions requiring 100% official language translation (e.g. Canadian French or EU compliance), preventing untranslated English leakage.
findings.recommendation: Retain MissingMessagePolicy::Reject as the default in regulated deployment configurations.

findings.description: Diagnostic::validate enforces that DiagnosticLocale::Custom(tag) must contain a hyphen ('-'), ensuring conformance to BCP 47 subtag standards and preventing unparseable locale identifiers.
findings.recommendation: Maintain BCP 47 hyphen validation on custom locale identifiers across all contract versions.

findings.description: The external evaluation protocol in evaluation/external-evaluation.json is contractually prepared and locked at prepared_not_preregistered; participant recruitment, formal pre-registration, ethics clearance, and live trial execution remain an open maturity gate.
findings.recommendation: Preserve gate T27-G-USABILITY-EVALUATION open until independent trial governance is established.

findings.description: ADR 0010 explicitly identifies that diagnostics and institutional governance are core architectural concerns, mandating stable machine codes, plain text/JSON/JSONL multi-format rendering, and default-deny policies without misrepresenting policy checks as legal or privacy advice.
findings.recommendation: Maintain the explicit boundary distinguishing software policy evaluation from formal legal compliance advice.

findings.description: evaluation/external-evaluation.json mandates living review update testing and adversarial provider fixtures, ensuring usability and stability are evaluated under stress rather than only clean synthetic datasets.
findings.recommendation: Ensure living-review updates and adversarial provider edge cases are executed during participant trials.

panel_recommendations: Retain strict zero ANSI escape sequence enforcement and explicit severity-word prefixes across all CLI/MCP diagnostic renderers.
Preserve machine identifier invariance (code, severity, blocking, evidence_ids) when expanding message catalogues to additional locales.
Maintain independent information specialist requirements (minimum 2 specialists, developer team exclusion, conflict disclosure) in trial pre-registration.
Preserve honest claim boundaries distinguishing source-verified diagnostics from external participant usability trials and full golden snapshot suites.
open_gates: Compile and run plain/JSON/JSONL snapshots and no-colour tests.
Create message catalogues and execute locale-fallback tests.
Complete keyboard, screen-reader and information-specialist usability evaluation.
